title: Canonical derived Hom restriction between opens of a ringed space
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. On its open-covering site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], write $\operatorname{moduleRings}(X)$ for its structure sheaf with commutativity forgotten, and use its sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $T$, let $r_T=\operatorname{overFunctor}(\operatorname{moduleRings}(X),T)$ be restriction to the slice site of opens contained in $T$, with the restricted ring sheaf. For $i:W\hookrightarrow U$, let $s_i=\operatorname{overMap}(\operatorname{moduleRings}(X),i)$ be further restriction. Use the standard additive, finite-limit-preserving and finite-colimit-preserving structures on these functors. Choose the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on $X,U,W$ in a common morphism universe. Put $R_T=D(r_T)$, $S_i=D(s_i)$, and let $e:R_U S_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R_W$ be the canonical isomorphism obtained from the inverse derived-composition isomorphism followed by the derived image of $r_U s_i\cong r_W$. For $E,F\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $a:R_U E\to R_U F$, define $\operatorname{derivedOpenHomRestriction}(X,i,a)=e_E^{-1};S_i(a);e_F$, a morphism $R_W E\to R_W F$. Here semicolons denote composition from left to right. This defines the canonical restriction of local derived Hom; it has no covering or vanishing hypothesis.

def derivedOpenHomRestriction (X : RingedSpace.{u}) {W U : Opens X} (i : W ⟶ U)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X).over U))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X).over W))]
    {E F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X))}
    (f : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ⟶
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj F) :
    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X) W).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ⟶
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X) W).mapDerivedCategory.obj F
